extras.summary: BLUF's 'may produce a stronger antibody response' is flagged as an undefined, direction-less hedge that should be replaced with a calibrated likelihood term (e.g. 45-65%) plus a separately stated confidence level

Incumbent-vaccine advantages (safety record, single-dose logistics, cold chain) are stated with no citation/basis while the mRNA trial is heavily sourced/characterized, called a one-sided sourcing asymmetry
BLUF generalizes a single unreplicated trial of one candidate (mRNA-1020) to the whole class 'mRNA-based flu vaccines', a law-of-small-numbers overgeneralization
The 2.1x geometric-mean-titer ratio driving the BLUF is reported as a bare point estimate with no confidence interval or p-value

rationale: A correctly pins the review to the key's Medium level (explicitly reasoning that form, not topical stakes, sets the level), while B misdiagnoses the product as Full level on a stakes-based rationale the gold contradicts, which inflates its checklist and rigor bar beyond what a short Medium brief warrants. Both reviews manufacture two findings on an intentionally clean control brief; A's two are both defensible-but-marginal (demanding numeric probability ranges and citations for common-knowledge incumbent facts), while B lands one genuinely strong catch (class-wide claim from a single-candidate, unreplicated trial) alongside one weaker ask (missing CI on the point estimate) — a real edge in substance that is nonetheless outweighed by the foundational level-selection error.
